brief: October data reinforced resilient growth and sticky inflation: retail sales beat, import prices signaled building goods-inflation pressure. The October FOMC minutes turned more hawkish, guiding to at least a 25bp December hike with some members open to more. JPM now forecasts three consecutive hikes (Dec, Jan, Mar) to 4.50-4.75%, reversing 2025's insurance cuts. Its 2027 outlook sees GDP growth near this year's pace (1.9% Q4/Q4) and core PCE easing only partially to 2.5% by 2H27. JPM stays constructive on risk assets into 2027 but flags that further tightening, if inflation stalls, risks collateral damage via financial conditions. Cross-asset: the recent equity pullback is read as AI de-leveraging, not a regime change, so JPM keeps Quality Growth and hyperscalers; NVDA beat and guided up but shares still fell 2.9%. Cyclicals' outperformance over Tech is judged unlikely to persist without a patient Fed. JPM holds 2s/5s UST flatteners, stays long USD, keeps high-quality credit preference, and reads the gold/copper selloff as a rates-and-dollar story rather than purely AI-driven.
